messages:
maria (PM): ok folks – quick thread to lock down acceptance for the Observability Console retention UX PRD. I want clear QA criteria, migration path, and any regulator/consent edge cases called out.

olivia (Design): high level: retention tiers + timeline picker + soft-warning for long retention. Need copy for privacy. Will post mock later.

devin (Eng): main constraints: indexes for traces and logs differ, purge jobs run on a different cadence. We'll need a migration job for customers moving to tiered retention. Also cost estimates per 1M tokens/day.

raj (SRE): SLO worry: if a customer picks 2y retention they may hit storage quotas. We should enforce a per-org storage cap or require Dedicated. Also audit log events for retention changes.

sam (QA): can we get a matrix of acceptance tests? e.g., change retention -> background job triggers -> data older than TTL purged within window -> UI shows 'deleting' state -> downstream billing updated.

maria (PM): yes. Draft acceptance checklist below. Please comment inline.

maria (PM): Acceptance checklist (draft):
- UI: user can select retention tier (7d, 30d, 90d, 1y, custom up to 2y).
- UI: when selecting >90d show privacy notice and require checkbox consent.
- API: patch /orgs/:id/settings/retention returns 202 and job_id when change accepted.
- Backend: migration job enqueues correct purge tasks, respects per-tenant rate limits.
- Data: traces/logs older than chosen TTL removed within 24h window after job completes.
- Observability: console shows estimated storage change and monthly cost delta pre-submit.
- Audit: change logged to org audit stream with actor, old_tier, new_tier, timestamp.
- Rollout: feature gated behind `console.retention_v2` flag for 10% canary.

devin (Eng): small nit: `24h window after job completes` -> we should say "within 24h of job start for shard X". Some shards backfill slower. I'll update.

olivia (Design): copy for privacy notice: "Longer retention stores more metadata and may affect regulatory data controls. Check with your compliance team." Keep short.

raj (SRE): also require an org-level confirmation for any retention extension that increases storage by >20% estimated. Prevent accidental bill shock.

maria (PM): good. Add that. Also, we need to detail export/backup edge cases: if customer has active exports into S3, purges should not delete exported copies but must mark the source data deleted.

sam (QA): test cases I want to own:
- Happy path: change 30d->90d for small org (10GB), job succeeds, UI shows new tier, data retention reflected in query results.
- Rollback: change 90d->30d immediately after upgrade, ensure purge job deletions happen and queries reflect new TTL.
- Partial failure: shard job fails for shard-3 -> UI shows partial state and job_id, alert to SRE.
- Billing calc: cost delta shown matches simulated billing within 5%.

devin (Eng): here's a sample retention API payload we'll support:

```json
{
  "retention_days": 90,
  "confirm_privacy_consent": true,
  "requester": "maria@redwood.ai"
}
```

devin (Eng): backend will return: {"job_id":"rj-2024-xxxx", "status":"enqueued", "est_storage_delta_mb": 3450} as JSON.

olivia (Design): UI state flow summary: select -> preview costs + warning -> confirm modal (checkbox + password reentry for >1y) -> toast + progress bar in org settings -> final success or actionable error.

raj (SRE): ops playbook items: automated alert if any retention job >48h, SRE runbook to escalate to infra team, and automatic rollback safeguard if >70% of shards error.

maria (PM): constraints / out-of-scope (for sprint 1): per-field retention, retention by project, exporting retention policy to infra-as-code. We'll scope those later.

sam (QA): question: how to simulate very large orgs in CI? We need a synthetic dataset generator and a way to mock long-running purge jobs without actually deleting prod. Suggest `retention-sim` harness.

devin (Eng): agree. I'll add a `retention-sim` mode to the purge worker that runs in dry-run and emits the same events. We'll gate it to non-prod.

maria (PM): regulatory note: EU customers with GDPR subject requests must still be able to delete data on demand even if retention longer. Add acceptance: `on-demand delete` supersedes retention.

olivia (Design): UI microcopy for that: "Data deletion requests override retention schedules. Learn more" -> link to policy.

raj (SRE): infra-bot: retention job created: rj-2045001301 for canary org.

infra-bot: rj-2045001301 status: enqueued -> running shard 1/6.

maria (PM): next steps: devin implement API + dry-run, sam build `retention-sim` tests, olivia finalize mocks and copy, raj add alerts and runbook, I'll prepare rollout plan and canary list. Can we aim for a 10% canary next Tue?

devin (Eng): target OK, will send PR for API by EOD tomorrow.

sam (QA): I'll prep test matrix and schedule a smoke for Tue morning.

olivia (Design): mock update in Figma by EOD.

raj (SRE): I'll add canary orgs and alerting.

maria (PM): awesome — I'll update the PRD with these acceptance items and link to this thread. Thanks all :rocket:
